stories.headline: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
stories.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all.
stories.why_it_matters: Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules.

Technical Implementation: As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all.
Deployment & Impact: Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear.

stories.headline: Multi‑Ratio Video Resizing for Mobile Feed and Marketing
stories.summary: Serdar Cellat , Yuchen Xie , Bernadette Marcu , Blaid Burgess , Cody Jarrett , Carlos Pereira , Qing Shi , Samuel Carvajal , Manuel Pamplona , Dorothy Jung , Feiko Ritsema , Benjamin Klein , Alex Woo , Eugene Lok , Anna Pulido , Rebecka Swe , Sanford Holsapple , Ranjith Kumar Shetty Introduction Clips in the Netflix mobile app. At Netflix, a crucial part of our mission is ensuring our content looks stunning on any device.

stories.headline: AMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in history
stories.summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su said in the company's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that Q3 2026 was "was the largest and most profitable in our history." stories.headline: OpenAI introduces program to reduce AI data center energy demand during peak hours
stories.summary: Electricity consumption is one of the biggest concerns that residents bring up whenever a data center is proposed in their community, which is why OpenAI is taking steps to minimize its impact on the local electricity grid. According to the company , its Grid Protectors Program aims to reduce the power consumption of its data centers as local demand increases, ensuring that the grid is not overwhelmed during peak hours.
stories.why_it_matters: Aside from ensuring that the lights remain on for everyone, it would also allow its data centers to connect to the grid and go online sooner instead of waiting for the additional power sources to come online. stories.headline: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
stories.summary: Advertisement Advertisement Skip to content Home About the Author Advertising/Speaking Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies November 2, 2026 6 Comments Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user’s Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet’s access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.
stories.why_it_matters: A report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said Google has severed ties with Videostrong Technology Co., a TV box manufacturer in China that GTIG and other industry experts concluded was responsible for including malware that enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in a botnet dubbed “XCPE” (named after one of the malware’s core code components). This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cybersecurity.

stories.headline: A Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering Framework with Automated Cluster Cardinality Estimation Ability
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.00159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fuzzy clustering provides a robust framework for handling ambiguous and overlapping data boundaries, yet its traditional formulation generates entirely dense membership assignments that limit noise resilience and prevent estimating the true number of clusters, when it is unknown. To address these limitations, we introduce in this paper the Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering (GSFC) framework, which incorporates a continuous sparsity penalty into the fuzzy objective function.
stories.why_it_matters: Because closed-form solutions are precluded by the simultaneous presence of fuzzifier and sparsity exponents, we propose an efficient primal-dual bisection search coupled with specialized analytic pathways to rigorously enforce the partition constraint while organically driving trace memberships to exact zero. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2611.00159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fuzzy clustering provides a robust framework for handling ambiguous and overlapping data boundaries, yet its traditional formulation generates entirely dense membership assignments that limit noise resilience and prevent estimating the true number of clusters, when it is unknown.
Technical Implementation: Furthermore, we integrate a virtual noise sink to insulate outliers from the rest of the data points.

Deployment & Impact: Extensive empirical evaluations across synthetic toy datasets, high-noise geometric stress tests, and real-world benchmarks (UCI wine dataset and hyperspectral images) demonstrate that GSFC effectively exceeds conventional fuzzy benchmarks while autonomously resolving cluster cardinality.

stories.headline: Learning to bid and bundle: a posterior-sampling agent for online retail
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.00165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An online retailer launching a perishable product bids for sponsored-search clicks, discounts a bundle with an always-stocked staple and displays its remaining stock, which raises willingness to pay. It knows neither how clicks respond to its bid nor how strong and dispersed its market is, and learns both over repeated seasons from data its own decisions censor: a zero bid reveals nothing about paid clicks, and choices follow only clicks.
stories.why_it_matters: We design a posterior-sampling agent for it. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: It knows neither how clicks respond to its bid nor how strong and dispersed its market is, and learns both over repeated seasons from data its own decisions censor: a zero bid reveals nothing about paid clicks, and choices follow only clicks.
Technical Implementation: In weak markets it gives up 12% to 23% of one season's revenue over 500 seasons, four to seven times less than drawing once per season.
Deployment & Impact: One discount per season removes waiting at a cost of 5.9% of clairvoyant revenue in a weak market and none in a strong one.

stories.summary: An n8n error workflow fires only when an execution fails. Unpublish a workflow and nothing runs, so nothing fails, so no alert.
stories.why_it_matters: Here is the liveness check I run on EC2. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
